name: pulsar-ide-julia
author: Morgan Rodgers
description: Julia language support for Pulsar via the JETLS language server

jetlsPath.title: Path to jetls
jetlsPath.description: Leave as `jetls` to use the PATH, falling back to `<julia depot>/bin/jetls`. Set an absolute path to override.

juliaPath.title: Julia executable
juliaPath.description: Optional. Sets `JULIA_APPS_JULIA_CMD` for the server, so `jetls` runs with this Julia instead of the one that installed it. Must be Julia 1.12 or newer. Leave empty to use the installing Julia.

channel.title: Communication channel
channel.description: `pipe` (default) talks to JETLS over a local socket, so anything the loaded code prints to stdout cannot corrupt the protocol. `stdio` uses stdin/stdout; JETLS's docs warn that a stray `println` or a package banner then breaks the connection.

threads.title: Julia threads
threads.description: Passed as `--threads=` to Julia. Use `auto`, a number, or `4,2` (default,interactive). Empty = Julia's default.

defaultEnvironment.title: Default environment
defaultEnvironment.description: Passed as `--project=`. Only affects files with no `Project.toml` above them (standalone scripts). Files inside a project always use that project's environment. Accepts a path, `~/path`, or `@name` for a shared environment.

juliaFlags.title: Extra Julia flags
juliaFlags.description: Comma-separated Julia runtime flags placed before `--`, e.g. `--heap-size-hint=4G`.

autoInstantiate.title: Auto-instantiate environments
autoInstantiate.description: What JETLS does when a file's environment needs instantiating (missing or outdated manifest, or packages not downloaded yet). `prompt` asks first (once per environment per session); `always` instantiates without asking, which can download packages, run build scripts and modify `Manifest.toml`; `never` leaves it untouched and shows a warning. Maps to `full_analysis.auto_instantiate`. Takes effect without a restart.

debounce.title: Analysis debounce (seconds)
debounce.description: Wait this long after a save before re-running full analysis (`full_analysis.debounce`).

formatter.title: Formatter
formatter.description: Which formatter JETLS uses (`formatter`). For a custom formatter use the JSON field below.

settingsJson.title: Additional JETLS settings (JSON)
settingsJson.description: A JSON object in the shape of `.JETLSConfig.toml`, merged over the settings above. Example: `{"diagnostic": {"patterns": [{"pattern": "lowering/unused-argument", "match_by": "code", "match_type": "literal", "severity": "off"}]}}`. A project's `.JETLSConfig.toml` still takes precedence.

initializationOptionsJson.title: Initialization options (JSON)
initializationOptionsJson.description: Static JETLS options sent once at startup, e.g. `{"n_analysis_workers": 2}`. Changing this needs a server restart.

outlineSignatures.title: Signatures in the outline
outlineSignatures.description: Label entries in the outline view with what JETLS reports about them, instead of just their name: function signatures, struct headers (`FunctionTest{F} <: AbstractTestFunction`) and field types. Julia code often defines one name many times.

outlineLocals.title: Arguments and locals in the outline
outlineLocals.description: Also list each function's arguments, local variables and loop blocks in the outline view. Off keeps the outline to functions, types and top-level definitions.

replJuliaPath.title: REPL: Julia executable
replJuliaPath.description: Julia to start in the terminal REPL. Empty uses `julia` from the terminal's PATH (so juliaup channels work).

replThreads.title: REPL: threads
replThreads.description: Value for `--threads` (a number or `auto`). Empty leaves Julia's default.

replEnvironment.title: REPL: environment
replEnvironment.description: Empty starts the REPL in the active file's project (nearest Project.toml, if any). Or give a directory, or `@.` / `@v1.12` / `@name`.

replFlags.title: REPL: extra Julia arguments
replFlags.description: Appended to the command as written, e.g. `-e 'using Revise'` (`-i` is added automatically so the REPL stays open) or `--color=yes`.

replSendVia.title: REPL: how to send code

enum.description: Terminal service: documented API, but the terminal package may ask you to approve the commands
Select the code and use the terminal package's run-selected-text command (no approval prompt)

replSendVia.description: How code reaches the terminal. Starting the REPL always uses the terminal service.

replBracketedPaste.title: REPL: send as a bracketed paste
replBracketedPaste.description: Wrap multi-line code in bracketed-paste markers so the Julia REPL takes it as a single paste. Try this if multi-line blocks misbehave. Only applies to the terminal service.

debugJuliaPath.title: Debugger: Julia path
debugJuliaPath.description: Julia executable that runs the debug adapter and your program. Empty uses `julia` from the PATH.

debugEnvironment.title: Debugger: environment
debugEnvironment.description: Empty: the project of the file being debugged (nearest Project.toml). Or `@v1.12`, `@name`, or a directory. DebugAdapter itself must be installed in the default global environment.

debugThreads.title: Debugger: threads
debugThreads.description: Passed as `--threads=`. Empty uses Julia's default.

debugFlags.title: Debugger: extra Julia arguments
debugFlags.description: Added to the Julia command line, e.g. `--check-bounds=yes`.

debugStopOnEntry.title: Debugger: stop on entry
debugStopOnEntry.description: Pause at the first line when you start debugging, even without breakpoints. Interpreted debugging is slow, so this is off by default.

debugLaunchArgumentsJson.title: Debugger: extra launch arguments (JSON)
debugLaunchArgumentsJson.description: A JSON object merged into the `launch` request, e.g. `{"args": ["--n", "3"]}`. A field set to `null` is removed. By default only `program` and `stopOnEntry` are sent.

debugExceptionFilters.title: Debugger: break on exceptions
debugExceptionFilters.description: Exception breakpoint filter ids offered by the adapter (the debug output lists them after a session starts), e.g. `error`.

debugOpenWorkspace.title: Debugger: open the workspace pane when debugging starts

debugOpenOutput.title: Debugger: open the output pane when the program prints

debugProgramArguments.title: Debugger: program arguments
debugProgramArguments.description: Command-line arguments for the debugged script (`ARGS`), split like a shell would, e.g. `--n 3 "a b"`.

debugCompiledMode.title: Debugger: compiled mode
debugCompiledMode.description: Run code that is not being stepped through compiled instead of interpreted. Much faster, but you cannot step into or break inside it. Use with the modules/functions setting below.

debugCompiledModules.title: Debugger: compiled modules or functions
debugCompiledModules.description: Modules or functions to run compiled, e.g. `Base`, `LinearAlgebra`. Passed as `compiledModulesOrFunctions`.

replWorkspace.title: REPL: show variables in the workspace pane
replWorkspace.description: Start the REPL with a small helper (julia/workspace.jl in this package) that reports the variables of `Main` to the Julia Workspace pane over a local socket. Read-only; needs Julia 1.9 or newer.

workspaceModule.title: REPL: module shown in the workspace pane
workspaceModule.description: The module whose variables the workspace pane lists for the REPL, such as `Main` or `Main.MyPackage`. The pane's module menu sets this; the special value `@follow` shows the module around the cursor in the active Julia editor.
